assets.title: The Bed Counter's Ledger
assets.author: an unnamed attendant before the Dawn
assets.text:
Twelve beds. Twelve clean blankets. Eleven cups.

Apprentice took a cup downstairs. Remind him tomorrow.

Twelve beds. Thirteen blankets. Someone expects company.

Instructions arrived from the Office. We are to keep everyone in their assigned places until the ceremony ends.

Twelve beds. Twelve blankets. No one sleeping.

Count again in the morning.

assets.title: Instructions for the Final Atlas
assets.author: the Unclosed Office, unsigned circular
assets.text:
Each road shall receive a destination. Each settlement shall receive a place. Each border shall receive an owner.

Unregistered valleys must be reported before dawn. Reports received after dawn will be considered impossible and returned to their sender.

Please refrain from moving during the completion ceremony. The Office cannot accept responsibility for persons entered under the wrong country.

Tomorrow, the map will be finished.

assets.title: On the Ownership of Handles
assets.author: Pella of the Blue Handle
assets.text:
My first handle was chosen by the woman who made me. It was a good handle. I used it for thirty years.

When it broke, the mender asked what kind I wanted. Nobody had asked before.

I chose blue. My maker would have preferred green. I think we could have discussed it over tea.

I would have poured.

assets.title: A Cup for Whoever Comes Next
assets.author: a Hearthkeeper's household, copied anonymously
assets.text:
We used to set an extra place at supper for travelers. Then we had three travelers and only one spare plate. Grandmother said the custom needed improvement.

Now we keep a clean cup beside the door. Whoever comes next may use it. Whoever comes after that may wash it.

Grandmother called this hospitality. Grandfather called it a successful division of labor. They agreed for nearly sixty years.

assets.title: A Letter Kept Warm
assets.author: Iven, recipient unnamed
assets.text:
I charged the scarf at the inn. It will keep its warmth until morning. There is a loose thread beside the clasp, so pull gently.

You said I never remember practical things. I remembered the scarf, the bread, and your terrible little spoon.

I meant to remember a better goodbye. You will have to accept this one until I return.

assets.title: Notes on Keeping Water
assets.author: caravan mender Sef Dapple
assets.text:
Shade the jar before you shade your boots. Boots complain less expensively.

Repair a crack before the journey. A cup repaired halfway across the wastes becomes a meeting of everybody's opinions.

I have seen a rain jar emptied by a careless child and by a very careful adult. The child admitted it sooner.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Safe travels.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Go safely.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Take care on the road.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Good travels to you.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: May you find a way home.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Mind your footing out there.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Good to see a traveler.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Welcome, traveler.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Good to see you.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Hello there. Safe road so far?

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: A traveler. Welcome.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: Come in from the road for a moment.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: I don't know enough to tell you.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: I've only heard pieces of that story.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: You'd need someone who knows more than I do.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: I don't have a useful account of that.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: I'd rather leave that question to someone who was there.

assets.speaker: citizen_fallback
assets.text: I couldn't tell you with any certainty.

assets.title: nails
assets.author: BizmasterStudios
assets.attribution_text: RPG Crafting Material Icons by BizmasterStudios. Source: https://opengameart.org/content/rpg-crafting-material-icons. License: CC-BY-4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Leave yourself a way back.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Keep the return route clear in your head.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Come back with enough strength for the last stretch.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Go carefully, and remember the stairs.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Leave a little of yourself for the journey home.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Good travels. You still have to come back from them.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A delivery to sort. Lift with both hands. Looking brave is no help to a dropped crate.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: They're sorting a delivery. Two hands to a crate, please.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A delivery to sort. Keep a good hold before trying to look impressive.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Those crates need carrying. Bravery isn't a substitute for both hands.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: We're sorting the delivery. A dropped crate doesn't care what you meant to prove.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: The square has a delivery to sort. Hold the weight properly before taking a step.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: The delivery has been received. A stack of crates that stays where you put it is a pleasant surprise.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: The crates have arrived. I appreciate supplies that stay where they're set down.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Delivery received. None of those crates has tried to follow me. I like that.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: The delivery is in. A quiet stack is an agreeable neighbor.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: The crates are staying in the square for now. Predictable cargo makes a pleasant change.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Everything's arrived. Those stacks are behaving better than some things I've met underground.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Your journal needs a way back as much as it needs a new discovery. Mark the stairs before you admire the ceiling.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Give the return route as much ink as the new discovery.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Mark the stairs for your guildmates before you write about the fine ceiling.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Your journal should help someone get home from the place you're describing.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A page about a mystery is useful. So is the page that tells you how to leave.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Leave the next Milewarden a way back. The marvel can have its own paragraph afterward.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Sit if you're staying. My neck has retired, too.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Sit down. My neck gets tired before the conversation does.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: If you've got a story, bring it down to sitting height.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: I've retired from craning my neck. Take a seat.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: You can stand if you like. I'll be listening from here.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Staying a while? Sit. The road won't object.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Blink still needs somewhere clear to put you. Remember that when you're frightened.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Blink needs a clear place to arrive. Fear doesn't make more room.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Before you Blink, look where you'll stand afterward.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A wall stays solid when you're frightened. Blink toward clear ground.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Find your landing place before you cast Blink.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Blink can get you out of trouble if you leave it somewhere clear to put you.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: My old crew argued over every meal. I miss the noise.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: My crew could turn supper into an argument. I still miss hearing them.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: I miss my old crew most at mealtimes. Nobody here argues quite the same way.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: We argued over every meal on the road. I'd gladly hear it again.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A quiet supper makes me remember my crew. We were never quiet over food.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: My companions found something to disagree about at every meal. I miss those voices.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: My old crew brought five flags and one cooking pot. We learned which one mattered when it rained.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: My crew carried five flags and a single cooking pot. Rain taught us which to worry about.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Five flags in our packs. One cooking pot. We kept the pot dry first.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: We brought five flags on the road and cooked in one pot. Bad weather made us practical.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Rain didn't care about our five flags. Supper depended on the one pot.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Our crew had five flags between us and one cooking pot. We all agreed about the pot when the rain came.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A gate opening is a chance to leave as well as a chance to go deeper.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: When a gate opens, remember the way out.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: An open gate gives you a choice. Leaving is one of them.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: You needn't go deeper every time you can.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A gate that lets you onward also gives you a moment to decide.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Take a breath at an open gate. Going home is still a journey.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Supper is being set out. No helmets at the table. That rule took my old crew years to learn.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Supper's being laid out. Helmets can sit somewhere else.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: There's a meal going out. Take the helmet off before you lean over a bowl.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: They're setting supper. My crew needed years to learn that helmets weren't tableware.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Supper beside the fountain. I hope nobody brings a helmet to the table.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: The table is being laid. We can eat without armor getting a place of its own.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Supper is over. The cups are drying. Nobody argued about watch duty. I could get used to that.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Supper's over. A quiet meal with no watch-duty argument still surprises me.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: The cups are drying, and nobody has assigned me the late watch. Good evening.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: We've finished eating. I enjoyed hearing no quarrel about who stayed awake afterward.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: The meal ended pleasantly. Nobody tried to trade watch duty for the last serving.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Supper's finished. A clean cup and no watch roster make a fine end to it.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A sword arm needs rest. Pride can wait beside it.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Rest the arm that holds the sword. You'll need it again.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A tired sword arm deserves a pause.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Your pride can keep watch while your sword arm rests.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: Give that arm time before the next fight.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: There's no shame in resting the hand you rely on.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: I once slept below a tower built for a sky with two moons. Its roof kept our rain out well enough.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: I slept beneath a tower made for two moons once. Its roof was quite good at keeping out our rain.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: That old tower had two moons in its carvings. I slept there dry enough beneath our sky.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: A tower from a two-moon world gave me shelter once. The roof didn't mind the difference.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: I once found a dry place under a tower whose builders knew two moons. A good roof travels well between worlds.

assets.speaker: retired_delver
assets.text: The tower I slept under was built beneath a sky with two moons. Our rain still stayed outside.

assets.title: A Place Left for Someone
assets.author: A traveler from {city_name}
assets.text:
We borrowed this cart for the road from {city_name}. When its wheel broke, we made a shelter of it. When the rain ended, we left the shelter for the next person.

The keeper called that a poor way to return a cart. The mender called it a useful second career.

Our last destination was {dungeon_name}. We left the name here so nobody would have to guess which ruin we meant.

assets.title: The Root Register
assets.author: An unsigned woodland register
assets.text:
The roots took the lower shelves first. We moved the books upstairs. The branches took the upper shelves next. We stopped calling it damage.

{city_name} keeps the living names. This register keeps a few older ones. Both lists have room for another entry.

Under {dungeon_name}, someone wrote that the trees remember every visitor. Someone else crossed it out. The ink has faded; the crossing-out has not.

assets.title: The Second Measure
assets.author: A Milewarden's field note
assets.text:
This stone was measured twice. The first surveyor counted the road from {city_name}. The second counted the footsteps of everyone who had walked it.

Their figures disagreed. Their stone did not move.

The margin names {dungeon_name}. A Milewarden has added: I am taking a fresh sheet. If the old surveyors kept a third account there, I mean to bring a copy home.

assets.title: Notice for an Unfinished Journey
assets.author: An old survey office
assets.text:
All journeys beginning at {city_name} must name their destination. Any traveler bound for {dungeon_name} must also name the destination after that.

Blank lines are provided below.

A later hand has written: leave one blank. It gives the road somewhere to go.

assets.title: The Borrowed Light
assets.text: In {city_name}, a winter ledger follows a lamp from house to house. Each keeper wrote who would need it next. The last old entry names {dungeon_name}; below it, someone has drawn an empty hook.
assets.landmark_text: The road marker carries a lamp-shaped scratch. The ledger says a light can belong to a route, even while one person holds it.
assets.book_text: Beside the lamp entries, a later hand wrote: clean the glass before you pass it on. Underneath, in smaller letters: yes, you too.
assets.witness_text: We say the light is borrowed, even when we made the lamp ourselves. Someone will need it after us. My grandmother showed me the entry for {dungeon_name}. She made me clean the glass too.
assets.author: The local archive of {city_name}

event_notes.text: After supper, someone washed the cups while another dried them. The keeper put a clean lamp beside the next stack.
The crates arrived. A neighbor wiped down the borrowed tools before passing them to the next pair of hands.

assets.title: Names Kept for Returning
assets.text: The oldest register in {city_name} leaves space after every name. It began with travelers going to {dungeon_name}; the empty space was meant for whatever they would call themselves on return. The town kept the custom when the ink faded.
assets.landmark_text: Names cut beside the road have a second, smaller line underneath. Most are empty. Beside one, someone carved: I came back. I still like my name.
assets.book_text: The town copy records a keeper refusing to close the register. A name could be corrected by its owner. Nobody else was allowed to decide that a journey was finished.
assets.witness_text: We keep a space for the returning name. If you visit {dungeon_name}, come back and tell us what you'd put there. Leave it empty if you like. I'll be glad to see you either way.
assets.author: The local archive of {city_name}

event_notes.text: At supper, the keeper learned a traveler's name. By the time the cups were gathered, half the table was using it.
The delivery arrived. The receiver signed the ledger, then asked the carter whether anyone was waiting for them at home.

assets.title: The Shared Measure
assets.text: The old survey at {city_name} counted water jars and places to rest along the road. Its last entry names {dungeon_name}. A later warden added a question beside it: who will open the door?
assets.landmark_text: The roadside marks belong to that survey. Their spacing measures the help a traveler could expect, rather than the length of a stride.
assets.book_text: A local margin explains the same measure. A filled water jar counts as one interval; a closed door counts as none. The keeper still asks households to leave room for a traveler.
assets.witness_text: My grandparents argued over the numbers, but both left water by the door. The register ends at {dungeon_name}. I wonder who was there to meet the last surveyor.
assets.author: The local archive of {city_name}

event_notes.text: The supper table is clear again. One stool stayed empty until a late traveler arrived. Nobody had to ask for it.
The carter delivered the supplies. Before counting the crates, a neighbor brought them water and a stool.

assets.text: I tried so hard.

assets.text: Please. I prepared.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Come back when you need somewhere to sit.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: There's a place to rest when you come back.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Go well. I'll be here when the road tires you out.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Come back with whatever story you can carry.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Rest here again when you need it.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Safe travels. We'll make room for you on your return.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: My grandmother said the Dawn lasted three days. Her sister said four. They argued until sunset.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Grandmother counted three days of Dawn. Her sister counted four. Neither would let the other have the last word.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Our family has two accounts of the Dawn: three days and four. Both are in the same book.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Grandmother insisted the Dawn lasted three days. Her sister added a fourth every time she told it.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Three days, Grandmother said. Four, said her sister. Their argument lasted longer than either account.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: I've copied both family accounts of the Dawn. If I choose three days or four, somebody's ghost will complain.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: A delivery is being sorted in the square. I offered to count the crates. They said I should count cups instead.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We're sorting a delivery in the square. Apparently my cup-counting doesn't qualify me to count crates.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The crates are being sorted. I offered to help and was sent back to the cups.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: A delivery's in the square. They know what belongs where better than I do.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: They're sorting the delivery. I shall stick to vessels I can carry in one hand.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The square is busy with crates. I offered to count them. My reputation for cups arrived before I did.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The delivery has been received. Those crates can wait a little while. Tired hands make poor knots.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The delivery's here. Let tired hands rest before tying another knot.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Those crates have arrived safely. They can wait while the people who carried them sit down.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The sorting is done for now. A crate has more patience than a tired back.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We've received the delivery. I hope its carriers find a seat before finding another job.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The crates are in. There's time to rest before deciding which one to lift next.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The fountain offers rest. Keeping the steps clean is my contribution.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: People come here worn out. I keep the steps clear so they can sit.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The water does its work. I do the sweeping.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Rest by the fountain. You needn't earn a place beside it.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: I tend the fountain and make sure there's room around it. Some days that means moving a very stubborn crate.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The fountain has heard more road stories than I have. I still like listening.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Some bells are waiting for people, too.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: A wrapped bell can wait a long time.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Some bells stay quiet until their traveler comes home.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We keep a bell for people we hope to see again.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: There's waiting in a quiet bell.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: A bell needn't ring to remind us of someone.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Your guild keeps asking what's beyond the next hill. I keep a cup here for when you come back to tell me.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Milewardens come back with new names for faraway places. I make sure there's a seat when they tell us.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Your maps go farther than my errands. Bring me a story when you return.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The guild can keep its ink. I'll keep a cup ready for the hand that brings it home.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: You and your guildmates always want another road. I want to hear how you got back from it.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: When a Milewarden returns, we hear about country nobody here has seen. I like to be ready for that.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Welcome to {city_name}. Take a breath. The road can wait.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: You've reached {city_name}. Come out of the road and catch your breath.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Welcome to {city_name}. There's no need to tell your story standing up.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: {city_name} has room for another traveler. Start with a little rest.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: First time in {city_name}? Rest your feet before you decide where to go next.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: This is {city_name}. You're welcome here. The dust on your boots can wait.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Rest first. You can tell me what happened afterward.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Sit for a moment. News keeps better than tired legs.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: You can finish that story after you've rested.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Let the road have a minute without you. Take a seat.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Rest your hands. Whatever happened, you don't have to tell it all at once.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: You look as though you've carried the journey far enough for today.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We set a place for whoever the road brings next.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Leave a place open. The road hasn't sent everyone yet.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: There's a cup for whoever reaches us next.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Someone we haven't met will need a seat.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We can make room when the next traveler comes.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Keep one place ready for a stranger.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We argue over who should mend a road. Then someone's child walks it, and suddenly everyone has a shovel.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Everyone has an opinion about a road until it needs mending. A child walking it usually settles the matter.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: A broken road becomes public business as soon as someone we know has to use it.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Neighbors can quarrel all morning and share a shovel before supper.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The loudest argument about a road often comes from two people who will mend it together.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: People disagree about who should do the work. They agree they want their neighbors to get home.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.condition: Met speaker; returned from a linked ruin
assets.text: Back from {dungeon_name}? Sit down before you tell me about it.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.condition: Met speaker; returned from a linked ruin
assets.text: You made it back from {dungeon_name}. Rest first; I can listen afterward.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.condition: Met speaker; returned from a linked ruin
assets.text: Back from {dungeon_name}? I was hoping to hear your steps again.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.condition: Met speaker; returned from a linked ruin
assets.text: Leave {dungeon_name} outside for a moment. You're back among neighbors.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.condition: Met speaker; returned from a linked ruin
assets.text: I've been wondering about your trip to {dungeon_name}. Sit while you tell me.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.condition: Met speaker; returned from a linked ruin
assets.text: So {dungeon_name} let you come home. Take a breath before the account.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We are setting out supper by the fountain. There is always room for another cup.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We're laying supper out by the fountain. Pull up a place while there's one spare.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Come eat with us by the fountain. I can find another cup.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: There's supper to set out and a traveler to fit in. That sounds right to me.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We're making room for supper. Bring yourself; we'll sort out the cups.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Supper is going out beside the fountain. A guest is easier to find than an excuse for an empty place.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Supper has finished. We leave the cups out to dry. Someone always remembers one more story while washing up.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The meal is over. The washing-up keeps producing more conversation.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Supper's finished, and the cups are drying. Somebody is still telling the story they started at the table.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We cleared supper away. Nobody seems ready to clear the last story away.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The cups are washed after supper. A few neighbors linger over the drying cloths.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: Supper has ended. I leave the cups out while people finish talking.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: When the worlds came together, my family brought a kettle and the name of their village. We've replaced the kettle twice. We still use the name.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: My family's village name survived the collapse. Their kettle lasted less well. We're on the third one now.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: When the worlds joined, my family kept their village's name and brought their kettle. Two kettles later, the name remains.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: The kettle my family carried from their old world is gone. So is its replacement. We still greet people with the old village name.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: My family brought a village name and a kettle into the Endless World. The name has needed fewer repairs.

assets.speaker: fountain_keeper
assets.text: We call this place by the village name my family saved at the collapse. The kettle they brought has been replaced twice.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Mind the corners on your way out.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Watch the corners. Fresh work deserves a little care.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Go carefully around the doorframe.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Safe travels. Give your seams a look before you leave.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Mind the edges on the road.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Take care of the things that carry you.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: A local delivery to sort. First the bindings, then the contents. A damaged handle tells you where to start.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The delivery's being sorted. I look at the bindings before I look inside.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: They're sorting crates. A worn handle usually tells me where to begin.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: A delivery in the square. First I check what held it together on the road.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The crates are being sorted. Look at their straps before trusting their weight.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: We're sorting the delivery. Good contents still need sound handles.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The delivery has been received. Those crates will stay here while we decide where everything belongs.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The delivery has arrived. We'll leave the crates here until there's a place for their contents.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Those crates are received. Unpacking can wait until we know where to put things.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The delivery's in. I'd rather plan a shelf than empty a crate onto the ground.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The crates will stand here for now. Deciding where things belong takes longer than opening them.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: We've received everything. The square can hold the crates while we sort out their next homes.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: If your guild writes about a strange old tool, draw the handle too. Someone held it. I'd like to know how.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: When you draw an old tool for the guild, show me the worn parts. That's where the hands were.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Copy the handle as carefully as the mysterious marks. Somebody had to hold the thing.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Your guild can tell me where a tool was found. I'd also like to know how its owner used it.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: If you bring back a sketch, leave room for the grip and the repairs.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: A strange tool still has weight and edges. Put those in your account; a mender will thank you.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Let me finish this seam. It has strong opinions.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: One moment. This seam keeps opening where I thought I'd finished.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Let me tie this off before we talk.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Hold your story a moment. I'm trying to persuade these edges to meet.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: I'll listen as soon as this stitch stops arguing.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: A moment, please. The seam has had more to say than the customer.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: An old enchantment can keep doing its job after everyone forgets what the job was.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Some enchantments keep working long after anyone remembers why they were made.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: An old working can outlast its instructions. That's when people bring it to me.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The maker dies, the job is forgotten, and the spell carries on. It can make repairs complicated.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: I ask what an enchantment was meant to do before I decide what has gone wrong.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: A spell can be perfectly obedient to an order nobody needs anymore.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Two households can spend a year arguing over a gate and still ask the same mender to fix it. I send each of them half the bill.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: A disputed gate still needs a sound hinge. I charge each household for half.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Neighbors arguing over a gate agree on one thing: I should mend it. Then they argue about the bill.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: I've repaired a gate while both households explained why it belonged to the other.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Two households can disagree over a gate for years. The wood doesn't improve while they wait.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: I mend the shared gate, send half the bill each way, and let the neighbors choose what to argue about next.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Supper is being set out. I inspect a cup before I fill it. Occupational habit.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Supper is going out. I always check a cup's rim before using it.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: They're setting supper by the fountain. I'll look for cracks before I pour anything.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The table is being laid. A quick look at the cups won't delay me long.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Supper's on its way out. I can't quite stop checking the handles.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: We're setting out a meal. I trust a cup more once I've turned it in my hand.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Supper has finished. Warm cups cool at their own pace. So do people.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The meal is over. Let the cups cool before putting them away.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Supper's finished. The cups and their users can take their time cooling down.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The table has emptied. I leave a warm cup alone for a little while.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: After supper, even a good cup deserves time on the shelf.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: We've finished eating. There's no hurry to pack warm cups together.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: That hinge came from a world with no iron. This door came from a world with too much of it. They fit. Took me most of a morning.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: I fitted an ironless world's hinge to a door from a world full of iron. It took most of the morning.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: That door and its hinge began in different worlds. One had too much iron, one had none. I made them meet by lunchtime.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: The hinge came from a world without iron. The door didn't. Most of a morning went into making them agree.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: Different worlds made that hinge and door. Their makers never had to worry about fitting them together. I did.

assets.speaker: relic_mender
assets.text: I spent most of the morning with a hinge from an ironless world and a door from one that had too much. They close properly now.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: There is a local delivery to sort. Every crate has a mark. I wish everyone marked their maps this clearly.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: They're sorting the delivery. Every crate has a legible mark. What a comfort.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The crates are being put in order. I'd like their marker to write on my maps.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A delivery to sort, and someone has labeled it properly. I appreciate that.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The delivery marks are clear. If only every road account were as easy to follow.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: They're sorting the crates in the square. A good mark saves a great deal of pointing.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The delivery has been received. The crates are still in the square. I recorded where they stand; nobody asked me to.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The delivery's arrived. I've written where the crates stand, though nobody required a map of them.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The crates are still in the square after delivery. I found myself noting their positions.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Delivery received. I've made a small plan of the crate stacks. Habit.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The crates have arrived and stayed put. I recorded their positions before realizing I had no reason to.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The square has received its delivery. My notes about where it stands are more precise than anyone asked for.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Supper by the fountain. I can keep a map folded for the length of a meal. Usually.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: There's supper by the fountain. The map can stay folded until I've eaten.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A meal by the fountain is a useful reason to put my papers away.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: We're having supper here. I shall try to leave the road out of the conversation for one bowl.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Supper is being set out. My map fits in its pocket better than beside a plate.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The fountain table is being laid. I've folded the map; that ought to count as being ready.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Supper is over. I learned that three people can disagree about a road without unfolding a single map.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The meal is over. We managed a road argument with every map still folded.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Supper finished before the argument about the road did.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: We ate by the fountain. Several people disagreed about a road they'd never put on paper.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The dishes are clearing. I've learned that folded maps don't prevent route disputes.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Supper's done. I kept the map away from the food, though I couldn't keep roads out of the talk.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: Safe roads. Soft landings.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: Safe travels, and gentle ground.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: May the road treat you carefully.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: Good roads. Watch the hard corners.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: Travel safely. I'm fond of an uneventful arrival.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: Mind your footing. I'll mind mine.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.condition: Future support; this individual has chosen their current handle
assets.text: I chose this handle. The first one was somebody else's idea.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.condition: Future support; this individual has chosen their current handle
assets.text: This handle was my choice. The one I started with wasn't.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.condition: Future support; this individual has chosen their current handle
assets.text: Someone else picked my first handle. I picked this one myself.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.condition: Future support; this individual has chosen their current handle
assets.text: I chose the handle I'm wearing now. It took a while for anyone to ask.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.condition: Future support; this individual has chosen their current handle
assets.text: My first handle came with me. This one came from a decision I made.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.condition: Future support; this individual has chosen their current handle
assets.text: I had a say in this handle. I'd like that remembered.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: I'm the courier. The soup is a separate arrangement.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: I'm here to deliver a message. Soup requires a separate agreement.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: Courier. Please address the letter, not the soup.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: I carry letters for a living. What I carry for supper is my business.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: I'm the courier you were waiting for. You weren't promised soup.

assets.speaker: potfolk_neighbor
assets.text: The delivery is a letter. Any soup is between me and the cook.

assets.title: Whose Light Remains
assets.author: The local archive of {city_name}
assets.text: You're a Milewarden, aren't you? Perhaps you can settle an argument. We pass a lamp from house to house, but the inscription in {dungeon_name} may tell a different story. Read our ledger before you go, then bring me the words you find there.
assets.ledger_prompt: Copy the lamp account from the town book in {city_name} before setting out.
assets.inscription: The keeper who tends this lamp owns it. After the keeper departs, the lamp passes to the next keeper as their own property.
assets.finding: Here the lamp is borrowed. There it belongs to whoever tends it. The two places kept different customs.
assets.completion: So they called it their own. My grandmother would have had words with them. I'll keep your copy beside ours. Let the next reader see both.

assets.title: A Space After the Name
assets.author: The local archive of {city_name}
assets.text: We leave a space after every traveler's name. Some say the old archive in {dungeon_name} did the same. Your guild goes to places the rest of us only talk about. Would you copy our register, read theirs, and tell me what you find?
assets.ledger_prompt: Copy the returning-name account from the town book in {city_name} before setting out.
assets.inscription: At departure the name is entered. At return the traveler may add a name or leave the second line empty.
assets.finding: Both registers let the traveler choose what to write on returning. Both allow the line to stay empty.
assets.completion: They left the choice to the traveler too. Good. I was hoping we hadn't forgotten something kind.

assets.title: The Third Measure
assets.author: The local archive of {city_name}
assets.text: The old wardens measured a road by the places where you could drink and rest. That's how our town book tells it. If your travels take you to {dungeon_name}, will you copy the archive inscription? Read our account first. I'd like to know whether they counted as we did.
assets.ledger_prompt: Copy the shared-measure account from the town book in {city_name} before setting out.
assets.inscription: A measure is entered only where water is offered and a traveler can rest.
assets.finding: Water and a place to rest count in both accounts. The old wardens used the same measure here and there.
assets.completion: Water and a place to sit. I'm glad those words lasted. I'll put your copy in the town book. Sit down while I find the ink.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: You came back.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: You returned.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: I remember you.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: You found me again.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: I waited for you.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Is it you?

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Stay where I can remember you.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Don't leave me.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Stay a little longer.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Stay in my sight.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Let me remember.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Wait with me.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: I had a name.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Someone knew my name.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: I remember a name.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: What was I called?

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: They called me something.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: My name was here.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Was it warm outside?

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Is the sun warm?

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Was there sunlight?

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Tell me about the warmth.

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Did you feel the sun?

assets.speaker: tomb_shade
assets.text: Is it cold outside?

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Visitors must wait outside.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Wait beyond the door.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: No visitors inside.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Remain outside.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Visitors halt here.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Entry is refused.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Inventory discrepancy.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Uncounted arrival.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Correct the count.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: One too many.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: You are unlisted.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Return to your place.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: That was accounted for.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: The count was correct.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: That changes nothing.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: I counted twice.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: The place was assigned.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: Nothing was missing.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: There were beds here. I counted them.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: I counted their beds.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: The beds stood here.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: They slept here once.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: I kept the blankets.

assets.speaker: crypt_skeleton
assets.text: I counted every bed.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A full cup deserves a steady hand.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Carry a full cup carefully.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Keep the water steady before you hurry.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A spilled cup is costly country out here.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Take your time with a full vessel.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Water is worth a steadier step.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: If you find more country, write down how you reached it.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Bring back the route as well as the name.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Write how you got there. Someone will want to follow.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Keep a note of the turns you take.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: If the road reaches unfamiliar country, leave a useful account.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Good travels, guildmate. Give your return route a page too.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The Office promised a complete map. We are still correcting their work.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The Office called its atlas final. Our margins keep growing.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: An Office clerk promised the last map. I'd like to show them my extra sheets.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: We still find the Office's old marks. We still have to check them.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The Office meant to finish the map during the Dawn. The roads have been uncooperative ever since.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Old Office maps have room for certainty. I prefer a margin for corrections.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The oldest oaks still wear the surveyors' nails.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Some old oaks have grown around the survey nails.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Those copper marks went into the trees before our maps.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The trees have kept the oldest survey marks.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: An oak can hold a surveyor's nail longer than a book holds its page.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Look for old nails where the bark has grown thick.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: We Milewardens map the roads and catalogue the mysteries along them. Copy what you find. Ask who remembers it. Leave the next guildmate a way home.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Milewardens bring back routes and accounts of strange things along them. A useful report helps the next traveler come home.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Our guild maps the world and catalogues its mysteries. Write the place down before you get lost admiring it.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: We carry maps out and bring corrections home. If you find something strange, copy what you can and name who told you the rest.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A Milewarden's journal holds roads, mysteries, and other people's accounts. Keep enough detail for a guildmate to follow your steps.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: We're here to map what we reach and learn what lives there. The next guildmate deserves more than a dramatic name.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Another Milewarden! I've put {city_name} on my map. Spelled it correctly this time.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A Milewarden in {city_name}. Good. I'd like another pair of eyes on this map.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Welcome, guildmate. I've written {city_name} clearly enough for once.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: {city_name} is on my map. Now there's another Milewarden to check the spelling.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: You've reached {city_name}, guildmate. Keep that name somewhere the rain won't find it.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A fellow Milewarden! I've just finished putting {city_name} in the right margin.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A guildmate. Good. Hold this corner of the map before the wind takes it.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Guildmate, could you hold this map flat? It wants to travel before I do.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A Milewarden. Good company for an unfinished map.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Come here, guildmate. This corner keeps folding over the place I'm trying to read.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Another journal on the road. Let me keep the wind off it.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Good to see a fellow Milewarden. Have you found a way to make paper ignore the weather?

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: An old border can outlive the kingdom that drew it. I ask the neighbors what they call a place before I put ink on the map.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Before I copy an old border, I ask who lives on each side of it.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A kingdom can vanish while its boundary stones remain. The neighbors still have to get along.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Two neighbors may name a place differently. My map has room for both names.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: I write down what the people here call their country. Old rulers rarely answer follow-up questions.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: A border on old paper is worth asking about. So are the households it crosses.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: There is a ruin called {dungeon_name} in the country near {city_name}.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: My notes place {dungeon_name} in the country near {city_name}.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: There's an old ruin near {city_name} called {dungeon_name}. I've written down the name.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: {dungeon_name} is the ruin named in my notes for the country around {city_name}.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: If you're asking about ruins near {city_name}, I have an account naming {dungeon_name}.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: I keep {dungeon_name} beside {city_name} in my road notes. That's the ruin people here refer to.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The multiverse collapsed into the Endless World. Every road we follow belongs to it now. I've filled nine maps and still haven't found a good place to stop.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: Countless worlds became the Endless World when the multiverse collapsed. I've filled nine maps of it. There's more road ahead.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The collapse joined the multiverse into one infinite world. Nine maps haven't made much of a dent in my pile of blank paper.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: We walk one world now, made from the worlds that collapsed together. I've filled nine maps and kept walking.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The Endless World is what remains of the collapsed multiverse. I have nine maps of places I've reached, and room for another.

assets.speaker: milewarden
assets.text: The multiverse came together in a single infinite world. Nine finished maps are sitting in my bag. The world is still ahead of me.
